Hello all,
I don't have many resources at the moment (traveling + internet is expensive) so I appreciate your help even though my question lacks research. I never used shiny but was briefly told what it can do. 

I am using R Markdown and Knitr to output HTML documents. I also have a database named "history.predict" (size 2.7 mb) which I want to embed into the html for my purpose.
I created this function which effectively subsets and plots a chart according to given CityCode (refers to different city of different states). City Codes are int ranging form 1 to 255 by increment of 1.

diet.graph_per.capita<- function(x){
total<- history.predict[history.predict$CityCode %in% x,]
total$Year<- as.numeric(total$Year)
capita<-ggplot(total, aes(x=Year, y=Total_Value, shape=Model, colour=Model_Class)) +
    geom_point(size=4)+
    labs(x = "Year",
         y = "Total Value (day)",
        title = paste("Total Value of City", x))+
        labs(colour="Scenario", shape= "Source")+
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = (seq(1965, 2100, by = 15)))
print(capita)
}

Is it possible that the html output has an interactive input value (that maps to the CityCode, or x input in function(x)), where whatever the selected CityCode is changed a graph is updated in the webpage? I hope this question is not extremely obvious, but if it is, or if I am missing an obvious structure, please redirect me :D
Thanks all!
